name: Rafael Candelaria
equipment: Leather duster, new, which he saved six months for and wears in all weathers
Carbine (Spencer, .56), the line's, kept under the roof seat
A long coach whip with a braided buckskin popper, given to him by Jethro Petree in 1878
Driving gloves, a slicker and a hat with a stampede string
Horse: Relámpago, a flea-bitten grey mustang he broke himself, who bites everyone but Rafael
A coach horn, brass, dented, which he blows coming into every station whether or not anyone is there
A lock of black hair in a locket, which is Ascensión Lucero's and which her grandfather does not know about
features: Both Sides of the River (Borderlands origin: speaks Spanish and English natively, knows the fords, trails and plazas of the Rio Abajo; advantage on Persuasion and Insight checks with border people of either side)

Saddle-Born (Cowhand: advantage on Riding checks, never disadvantage on ranged attacks from the saddle, mounts and dismounts with 5 ft of movement; his horse Relámpago is part of him: +15 hit points, never spooks under him, comes to his whistle from half a mile and acts on his initiative; proficient with the lariat)
Rawhide (Cowhand: advantage on saving throws against exhaustion, heat and cold; rides or drives 12 hours a day without forced-march saves; spends one extra Hit Die on a short rest)

Cow Sense (Cowhand, 2nd level: advantage on Animal Handling checks with cattle, horses and mules, which on the box means a six-horse team; turns the leaders of a stampede or a bolting team with a single check as an action, with advantage)

Outfit: Bronc Buster (Cowhand, 3rd level: breaks a wild or green horse in a day; stays mounted on any horse that tries to throw him or is shot from under him with a DC 10 Riding check, and on the box of any coach that is still on its wheels; takes no damage when a horse falls with him)

The Mail Road (Stage Driver background: knows every station, grade, ford and ambush place from Albuquerque to Plata Vieja; station keepers and hostlers feed him, change his horses and tell him who rode through; drives any team without a check in ordinary conditions)

personality.traits: I talk too much, laugh too loud and blow the horn too often. I believe the best of everyone until they make it impossible, and sometimes after that. I am in love, and everyone knows it but her grandfather.
personality.ideals: A driver gets them there. Passengers, mail, the box, the horses. However bad the road, however late, he gets them there.
personality.bonds: Jethro Petree, who taught me to drive and is the nearest thing I have had to a father since mine died. Ascensión Lucero. La Doña, which I have been learning to drive for three years and was going to drive one day.
personality.flaws: I saw Jethro talking to a fat man in a straw hat outside the Paragon House on 24 June and thought nothing of it, and I saw him stop the team before the bend, and I have said nothing, because I cannot bear to think it.

appearance: A slim, quick, handsome young man of twenty-two with curly black hair, a wide white grin, a scar on his chin from a fall off the box at sixteen, and hands much older than the rest of him. New duster, a red neckerchief, a black hat with a stampede string, and a whip coiled over his shoulder.
backstory: Rafael Candelaria was born in 1859 in Albuquerque's Old Town, the youngest of nine children of a carter who died when Rafael was ten. He went to work in the Rio Seco line's Albuquerque corral at twelve, mucking stalls, and old Jethro Petree saw how the boy handled the horses and took him onto the box. For nine years Jethro has taught him everything: how to hold six lines in two hands, how to take the Ceja grade in the wet, how to sing a frightened team quiet. Since 1878 Rafael has been the relief driver, riding the roof on the long runs and taking the lines on the easy stretches. He had hoped to drive la Doña himself one day. The railroad came instead. The Company has offered him a job on its buckboard line at $40 a month, and he hasn't answered. On the last run he is up on the roof with the mail sacks, and he sees everything at the Puerto de Piedra, including the thing he will spend two weeks trying not to have seen. (Companion. Hooks: Jethro; the halt before the bend; Ascensión Lucero; la Doña and the last run.)

dmNotes.roleplaying: Rafael is the line's heart and its future that will never happen: young, brave, cheerful and devoted to an old man who has betrayed everything Rafael believes in. Use him on the coach, as its driver if Jethro cannot or will not drive, and as the witness to the halt before the bend (CLUE F1). His arc is learning the truth about Jethro and deciding what to do with it. Let him lie for Jethro once, at the inquest, and be unable to do it again. In st-scenario-004, if Jethro drives, Rafael rides beside him on the box, and that is a scene.
dmNotes.voice: Quick, warm, half Spanish and half English in the same sentence, with a coach driver's vocabulary for horses and weather and a love-struck boy's for everything else. Calls Jethro "viejo" with enormous affection. Blows the horn when he is happy and when he is frightened.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: get the coach there, every time. Secondary: Jethro, and the truth about him, which he wants and dreads. Tertiary: Ascensión, and her grandfather's good opinion, which he will not get by driving for the Company.
dmNotes.secrets: He saw Jethro with Fenton Rusk outside the Paragon House on 24 June, and he saw Jethro halt before the bend. He told nobody. At the inquest he starts to say it and stops. A party that is kind to him, and does not make him choose between Jethro and the truth in public, can have both facts from him in st-scenario-001 or 002 (CLUES F1, C6 corroboration). He has also been meeting Ascensión Lucero at the acequia at night, and she has told him that her grandmother hates the Company and that her grandfather keeps the Company's papers in the iron safe in his office.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: friendly at once, eager to please, especially with anyone who can drive or handle horses. Toward Jethro: love, and then grief, and then love again if Jethro earns it on the last run. Toward Cyprian Ludlow: reverence. Toward Tabitha Lockhart, if played: a little afraid of her and very respectful. Toward Royal Penhallow, if played: an elder brother who shoes his horses. Toward the Company: he wants to hate it and needs its job.
